name: Meeting language: getting through meetings
description: Phrases for jumping in, checking what people mean, pushing back, handling questions you can't answer, agreeing next steps and coping with online calls.

words.term: Can I just jump in here?
words.definition: A friendly, common way to interrupt when the conversation is moving fast and you need to say something now.

examples.en: Can I just jump in here? That change also affects the mobile app.
examples.zh: 我能插一句吗？那个改动也会影响手机应用。

words.note: just 让语气更软，非常常用。不要说 'Let me interrupt you'，听起来很生硬。

words.term: Sorry to interrupt, but …
words.definition: A polite way to cut in when someone is still talking, usually to correct something or add something important.

examples.en: Sorry to interrupt, but the finance app is still on-prem.
examples.zh: 抱歉打断一下，财务系统还在本地机房。

words.note: 打断后要马上说重点，不要铺垫太长。

words.term: Can I add something?
words.definition: A simple way to ask for a turn when there's a pause in the discussion.

examples.en: Can I add something? The service desk will need training too.
examples.zh: 我能补充一点吗？服务台也需要培训。

words.note: 不用等别人点名才说话；看到空隙就用这句。

words.term: Just to add to what … said, …
words.definition: Use this to build on a colleague's point and show you were listening.

examples.en: Just to add to what Sarah said, we'll also keep a copy in a second region.
examples.zh: 补充一下 Sarah 刚才说的，我们还会在另一个区域保留一份副本。

words.note: 提到对方名字，显得尊重、有团队感，新西兰职场很看重这一点。

words.term: Just one quick thing from me.
words.definition: Signals that your point is short, so people are happy to give you the floor.

examples.en: Just one quick thing from me. The test environment is down tomorrow morning.
examples.zh: 我这边就说一件小事，测试环境明天上午停用。

words.note: 站会、例会收尾时特别好用。说了 quick 就真的要简短。

words.term: Building on that, …
words.zh: 在这个基础上，…（接着别人的想法往下说）
words.definition: Use this to take someone's idea one step further.

examples.en: Building on that, we could turn on the firewall rules at the same time.
examples.zh: 在这个基础上，我们可以同时把防火墙规则也打开。

words.note: 比 'And I think…' 更自然地把你的话和别人的观点连起来。

words.term: If I could just finish my point, …
words.definition: A polite but firm way to keep talking when someone cuts you off.

examples.en: If I could just finish my point, the logs also show the database timing out.
examples.zh: 让我先把话说完，日志还显示数据库超时了。

words.note: 语气平静就不会失礼。被打断时不要直接停下不说，这是很多中国同事的习惯。

words.term: Sorry, I didn't quite get to finish.
words.definition: Use this to get back to a point you were making before someone moved the meeting on.

examples.en: Sorry, Tom, I didn't quite get to finish. It'll only take a minute.
examples.zh: 抱歉 Tom，我刚才还没说完，一分钟就好。

words.note: quite 让语气更委婉，不像在抱怨别人打断你。

words.term: Can I come back to …?
words.definition: Use this to return to a topic the meeting already moved past.

examples.en: Can I come back to the licence costs? I don't think we finished that.
examples.zh: 我能回到许可证费用的话题吗？我觉得那个还没讨论完。

words.note: 适合在 'any other business' 或会议结束前用。

words.term: Going back to what … said earlier, …
words.definition: Brings back an earlier point, often one that nobody picked up.

examples.en: Going back to what Mei said earlier, I think user training should be in the plan.
examples.zh: 回到 Mei 之前说的，我觉得用户培训应该放进计划里。

words.note: 也可以用来帮不爱发言的同事的好观点被大家听到。

words.term: Before we move on, …
words.definition: Use this to stop the meeting going to the next item until you've said something.

examples.en: Before we move on, can I just check the go-live date?
examples.zh: 进入下一项之前，我能确认一下上线日期吗？

words.note: 时机很关键：在主持人说 'moving on' 的那一刻就说。

words.term: Sorry, go ahead.
words.definition: Use this when you and someone else start talking at the same time and you let them speak first.

examples.en: Oh, sorry, go ahead. I'll come in after you.
examples.zh: 哦，抱歉，你先说，我等下再说。

words.note: 让完之后要记得回来说你的话，可以加一句 'I'll come in after you'。

words.term: Can I stop you there for a sec?
words.zh: 我先打断一下（有紧急或重要信息时）
words.definition: A stronger interruption, used when people are going the wrong way and you need to stop them now.

examples.en: Can I stop you there for a sec? The certificate expired an hour ago.
examples.zh: 我先打断一下，证书一小时前就过期了。

words.note: 比 jump in 更强硬，用在故障处理或明显出错时。sec = second，口语。

words.term: On that point, …
words.definition: Connects what you say directly to what was just said, so your interruption feels relevant.

examples.en: On that point, the vendor told us the new version is due in March.
examples.zh: 关于这一点，供应商说新版本三月份出。

words.term: That's a good point, and …
words.definition: A positive way to take the floor: praise the last speaker, then add your idea.

examples.en: That's a good point, and it also means we'll need fewer licences.
examples.zh: 说得好，而且这也意味着我们需要的许可证会更少。

words.note: 用 and 而不是 but，听起来是合作而不是反驳。

words.term: I'll be quick.
words.definition: Promises you'll only take a moment, which makes people more willing to let you speak.

examples.en: I know we're short on time, so I'll be quick.
examples.zh: 我知道时间不多了，我很快说完。

words.term: Can I bring us back to …?
words.zh: 我们能回到…上来吗？（会议跑题时）
words.definition: Use this when the discussion has drifted and you want to return to the main topic.

examples.en: Can I bring us back to the cutover plan? We've only got ten minutes.
examples.zh: 我们能回到切换计划上来吗？只剩十分钟了。

words.note: 加上剩余时间做理由，就不会显得你在批评别人跑题。

words.term: Just a quick correction: …
words.definition: Use this to fix a wrong fact someone said, without making a big deal of it.

examples.en: Just a quick correction: the VPN's set up, but it hasn't been tested yet.
examples.zh: 小小更正一下：VPN 配好了，但还没测试。

words.note: quick 让纠正听起来不像在挑错，适合当着客户面纠正自己同事。

words.term: Could I just come in on that?
words.zh: 这一点我能说两句吗？（较正式）
words.definition: A slightly more formal way to ask to speak, good for steering meetings with senior people.

examples.en: Could I just come in on that? It goes against what we decided last month.
examples.zh: 这一点我能说两句吗？这和我们上个月的决定相矛盾。

words.note: come in on sth 是英式说法，在新西兰、英国会议里很常见。

words.term: Let me just finish this bit, then …
words.zh: 我先把这部分讲完，然后…
words.definition: Use this when someone asks a question mid-explanation and you want to answer it a bit later.

examples.en: Good question. Let me just finish this bit, then I'll cover cost.
examples.zh: 好问题。我先把这部分讲完，然后再讲成本。

words.note: 先肯定问题，再推迟回答，对方不会觉得被忽视。

words.term: Picking up on what … said, …
words.definition: Another way to link your point to an earlier speaker's idea.

examples.en: Picking up on what Aroha said, the same problem happens on the test site.
examples.zh: 接着 Aroha 说的，测试站点也有同样的问题。

words.term: I was going to say …
words.zh: 我刚才想说的是…（被抢话后重新开口）
words.definition: Use this to restart a point after someone else spoke at the same moment as you.

examples.en: I was going to say, we could test it on Friday instead.
examples.zh: 我刚才想说的是，我们可以改成周五测试。

words.term: Sorry, I've been trying to get a word in.
words.definition: A light, honest way to say you've been waiting for a chance to speak.

examples.en: Sorry, I've been trying to get a word in. I think we're missing testing time.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我一直想插句话。我觉得我们漏了测试时间。

words.note: get a word in = 插上话。语气轻松地说，大家会笑一下然后让你说。

words.term: There's one thing I'd like to raise.
words.definition: A clear way to bring up a new issue, often one that isn't on the agenda.

examples.en: Before we finish, there's one thing I'd like to raise about security.
examples.zh: 结束之前，我想提一件关于安全的事。

words.note: raise an issue = 提出问题。不要说 'I want to put forward a problem'。

words.term: Can I give a bit of context here?
words.definition: Use this when the group is missing background information that you know.

examples.en: Can I give a bit of context here? We tried this approach last year.
examples.zh: 我能补充一点背景吗？我们去年试过这个办法。

words.term: Can I add a slightly different angle?
words.zh: 我能从另一个角度说说吗？
words.definition: A soft way to bring in a different view without saying the other person is wrong.

examples.en: Can I add a slightly different angle? Separate subscriptions would make billing clearer.
examples.zh: 我能从另一个角度说说吗？分开订阅会让账单更清楚。

words.note: slightly 让分歧听起来很小，适合对客户或领导用。

words.term: Sorry, could you say that again?
words.definition: The simplest, most natural way to ask someone to repeat something.

examples.en: Sorry, could you say that again? I missed the date.
examples.zh: 抱歉，能再说一遍吗？我没听到日期。

words.note: 不要说 'Pardon?' 太多次，也不要只说 'What?'（不礼貌）。说明漏听了哪部分更好。

words.term: Could you slow down a little?
words.definition: Use this when someone is talking too fast for you to follow.

examples.en: Sorry, could you slow down a little? I want to get this right.
examples.zh: 抱歉，能说慢一点吗？我想把这个弄清楚。

words.note: 完全没问题，母语者也常这样说。加理由 'I want to get this right' 显得认真负责。

words.term: Sorry, you cut out for a second. Could you say that again?
words.zh: 抱歉，你刚才断了一下，能再说一遍吗？
words.definition: Use this on a call when the other person's audio drops and you miss what they said.

examples.en: Sorry, you cut out for a second. Could you say that again?
examples.zh: 抱歉，你刚才断了一下，能再说一遍吗？

words.note: 把原因归到网络上，对方不会觉得是你听力不好。

words.term: What do you mean by …?
words.definition: Asks someone to explain a word or idea that could mean different things.

examples.en: What do you mean by 'fully resilient'? Do you need it to survive a region outage?
examples.zh: 你说的“完全高可用”具体是指什么？需要能扛住整个区域故障吗？

words.note: 语调要上扬、友好，否则听起来像在质疑对方。

words.term: So you're saying …?
words.definition: Checks you've understood by repeating the main idea in your own words.

examples.en: So you're saying go-live depends on the pen test and the sign-off?
examples.zh: 所以你的意思是上线取决于渗透测试和签字确认？

words.note: 这是确认理解最有效的办法，对方会纠正或说 'Exactly'。

words.term: Just to check I've got this right, …
words.zh: 我确认一下我理解得对不对，…
words.definition: A polite lead-in before you sum up what someone said.

examples.en: Just to check I've got this right, the batch job starts before the sync finishes?
examples.zh: 我确认一下我理解得对不对，批处理是在同步完成之前开始的？

words.term: Sorry, what does … stand for?
words.definition: Use this when someone uses an acronym you don't know.

examples.en: Sorry, what does ADR stand for?
examples.zh: 抱歉，ADR 是什么的缩写？

words.note: IT 行业缩写极多，问一下很正常，别人往往也不知道。stand for = 代表。

words.term: Could you give me an example?
words.definition: Use this when a request or idea is too general to act on.

examples.en: Could you give me an example of what users find hard?
examples.zh: 能举个例子说明用户觉得哪里难用吗？

words.note: 收集需求时特别好用，把模糊的话变成具体的事。

words.term: Sorry, I didn't catch the last part.
words.zh: 抱歉，最后那部分我没听清
words.definition: Tells the speaker exactly which part you missed, so they don't repeat everything.

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't catch the last part. Was that Tuesday or Thursday?
examples.zh: 抱歉，最后那部分我没听清，是周二还是周四？

words.note: catch = 听清。比 'I didn't understand' 好，因为问题在“听”，不在“懂”。

words.term: When you say …, do you mean … or …?
words.definition: Offers two possible meanings so the other person can quickly pick one.

examples.en: When you say all users, do you mean all staff or just managers?
examples.zh: 你说所有用户，是指全体员工还是只有经理？

words.note: 给出选项比开放式提问更快得到答案。

words.term: Sorry, I'm a bit lost.
words.definition: An honest way to say you can't follow the discussion any more.

examples.en: Sorry, I'm a bit lost. Which server are we talking about now?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我有点跟不上了。我们现在说的是哪台服务器？

words.note: 说出来比假装听懂好得多，后面出错的代价更大。

words.term: Could you spell that for me?
words.definition: Use this for names, server names or anything you need to write down exactly.

examples.en: Could you spell that for me? I want to get the email right.
examples.zh: 能帮我拼一下吗？我想把邮箱写对。

words.term: Let me just repeat that back.
words.definition: Use this after instructions or numbers, to check you've got them right.

examples.en: Let me just repeat that back: secret first, then restart the function app.
examples.zh: 我复述一遍：先加 secret，再重启 Function App。

words.term: Did I get that right?
words.definition: A short question to put at the end of your summary.

examples.en: Three tenants, merged into one by Q2. Did I get that right?
examples.zh: 三个租户，第二季度前合并成一个。我理解得对吗？

words.term: Which one are we talking about now?
words.zh: 我们现在说的是哪一个？
words.definition: Use this when people say 'this one' or 'the other one' and you're not sure what they mean.

examples.en: Sorry, which one are we talking about now, the VPN or the firewall?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我们现在说的是哪一个，VPN 还是防火墙？

words.term: Could you put that in the chat?
words.definition: Useful on calls for names, links, numbers or words you can't catch.

examples.en: Could you put that in the chat? I still didn't catch the name.
examples.zh: 能打在聊天框里吗？我还是没听清那个名字。

words.note: 重复两次还没听清时用这句，很自然，不尴尬。

words.term: Could we go through that in plain English?
words.zh: 能用通俗的话再讲一遍吗？
words.definition: Asks for a simpler explanation without jargon, often for the client's sake.

examples.en: Could we go through that in plain English for a second?
examples.zh: 能用通俗的话再讲一下吗？

words.note: plain English = 不带术语的大白话。说是为了客户，自己也能听懂。

words.term: Was that fifteen or fifty?
words.definition: Checks a number that is easy to mishear, like teen and ty numbers.

examples.en: Sorry, was that fifteen or fifty thousand?
examples.zh: 抱歉，是一万五还是五万？

words.note: -teen 重音在后，-ty 重音在前；不确定就说 'one-five' 确认。

words.term: I'm not familiar with …
words.definition: A polite way to say you don't know a term, tool or process.

examples.en: I'm not familiar with your TDA process. How long does it usually take?
examples.zh: 我对你们的 TDA 流程不太熟悉，一般要多长时间？

words.note: 比 'I don't know' 更专业，后面接一个问题效果最好。

words.term: Just so we're all clear, …
words.definition: Use this to confirm a decision or meaning for the whole group, not just you.

examples.en: Just so we're all clear, the rollout is on hold until March?
examples.zh: 为了大家都清楚，推广暂停到三月对吗？

words.term: Could you give me a quick recap?
words.definition: Use this when you missed part of the discussion and need the main points.

examples.en: Sorry, I missed the start. Could you give me a quick recap?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我错过了开头。能简单概括一下吗？

words.note: recap = recapitulate 的口语简写。

words.term: What would that look like in practice?
words.zh: 那实际做起来是什么样的？
words.definition: Asks someone to turn a general idea into real steps or examples.

examples.en: More automation sounds good. What would that look like in practice?
examples.zh: 多做自动化听起来不错，实际做起来是什么样的？

words.term: Sorry, I haven't heard that expression before.
words.zh: 抱歉，我没听过这个说法
words.definition: Use this when someone uses slang or an idiom you don't know.

examples.en: Sorry, I haven't heard that expression before. Do you mean it was messy?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我没听过这个说法，你是说很乱吗？

words.note: 新西兰人很爱用俚语（sweet as、dog's breakfast），问一下大家都乐意解释。

words.term: Could you walk me through …?
words.zh: 能带我一步步过一下…吗？
words.definition: Asks someone to explain a process or design step by step.

examples.en: Could you walk me through how the failover works?
examples.zh: 能带我一步步过一下故障切换是怎么运作的吗？

words.term: Sorry, you lost me at …
words.zh: 抱歉，从…那里开始我就没跟上了
words.definition: A casual way to show exactly where you stopped understanding.

examples.en: Sorry, you lost me at the service mesh part.
examples.zh: 抱歉，从服务网格那部分我就没跟上了。

words.note: 口语、随意，适合同事之间；对客户用 'I'm not quite following' 更稳妥。

words.term: Roughly when do you need it by?
words.definition: Turns a vague 'soon' or 'ASAP' into a real deadline.

examples.en: No problem. Roughly when do you need it by?
examples.zh: 没问题。大概什么时候需要？

words.note: 别人说 ASAP 时一定要问，否则你会以为是今天，其实可能是下周。

words.term: I see your point, but …
words.definition: A polite way to disagree: show you understand first, then give your view.

examples.en: I see your point, but I'd still take a backup before the upgrade.
examples.zh: 我明白你的意思，但升级前我还是会备份。

words.note: 比直接说 'I disagree' 柔和得多，新西兰职场更习惯这种方式。

words.term: I agree with …, but …
words.definition: Use this when you agree with part of an idea but not all of it.

examples.en: I agree with the idea, but I'm not sure about the timing.
examples.zh: 我同意这个想法，但对时间安排不太确定。

words.note: 先说同意的部分，对方更愿意听你后面的意见。

words.term: I'm not sure about that.
words.zh: 这个我不太确定（委婉的不同意）
words.definition: A soft way to disagree. Native speakers often mean 'I don't think that's right.'

examples.en: I'm not sure about that. Even small changes can break things.
examples.zh: 这个我不太确定，小改动也可能出问题。

words.note: 英语母语者常用它表示委婉反对；别人对你这么说时，也要听出是不同意。

words.term: I'm a bit worried about …
words.definition: Raises a concern in a calm, non-confrontational way.

examples.en: I'm a bit worried about giving everyone admin rights.
examples.zh: 我有点担心给每个人管理员权限。

words.note: a bit 让担心听起来不夸张，但大家都会认真对待。

words.term: That's true, but …
words.definition: Accepts a fact, then adds the part the other person missed.

examples.en: That's true for small workloads, but with our traffic it might cost more.
examples.zh: 小负载确实如此，但以我们的流量可能会更贵。

words.term: How about … instead?
words.zh: 改成…怎么样？（提出替代方案）
words.definition: Offers an alternative, which makes a 'no' feel more helpful.

examples.en: How about we shut it down at night instead?
examples.zh: 改成晚上关掉怎么样？

words.note: 拒绝时最好附带一个替代方案，这样不像在唱反调。

words.term: … is going to be tough, sorry.
words.zh: …恐怕很难做到（委婉拒绝时间）
words.definition: A soft way to say a date or request isn't possible.

examples.en: Tomorrow's going to be tough, sorry. Could Thursday work?
examples.zh: 明天恐怕很难，抱歉。周四可以吗？

words.note: 不要直接说 'I can't'。用 tough 再给出新时间，对方很容易接受。

words.term: That's not part of the current scope.
words.zh: 这不在目前的项目范围内
words.definition: Use this when a client asks for extra work that isn't in the agreed project.

examples.en: That's not part of the current scope, but I'm happy to get you a quote.
examples.zh: 这不在目前的项目范围内，但我可以给你单独报价。

words.note: 顾问必备。后面加 'but happy to…'，既守住范围又保持合作。

words.term: I'd really recommend …
words.definition: Use this to stand firm on your professional advice in a polite way.

examples.en: I'd really recommend two weeks for testing.
examples.zh: 我强烈建议测试留两周时间。

words.note: really 加重语气但不失礼，后面最好给出过去的经验作为理由。

words.term: I'm not comfortable with …
words.zh: 我对…不太放心 / 我不太能接受…
words.definition: A professional way to refuse something you think is wrong or risky.

examples.en: I'm not comfortable promising that date to the client.
examples.zh: 我不太能接受向客户承诺那个日期。

words.note: 很有分量的一句话，对上级说也不失礼。

words.term: Can I play devil's advocate for a sec?
words.zh: 我唱个反调可以吗？（故意提反面意见）
words.definition: Use this to question an idea everyone seems to agree on, without sounding negative.

examples.en: Can I play devil's advocate for a sec? What if the vendor goes under?
examples.zh: 我唱个反调可以吗？如果供应商倒闭了怎么办？

words.note: 先打招呼说是“唱反调”，大家就不会觉得你在针对谁。

words.term: As long as …
words.zh: 只要…就行（有条件地同意）
words.definition: Agrees to something, but only if a condition is met.

examples.en: I'm fine with that, as long as we set up Intune first.
examples.zh: 可以，只要我们先配置好 Intune。

words.term: I take your point, but I still think …
words.zh: 你说的有道理，但我还是认为…
words.definition: Use this to hold your position after someone challenges you again.

examples.en: I take your point, but I still think we need the extra licences.
examples.zh: 你说的有道理，但我还是认为需要额外的许可证。

words.note: 被反驳时不要马上让步；用 still 表示你考虑过了，仍坚持。

words.term: I'd rather not … until …
words.definition: Pushes back by naming what needs to happen first.

examples.en: I'd rather not start building until we have the main requirements.
examples.zh: 在拿到主要需求之前，我不太想开始开发。

words.term: Honestly, that's not realistic by …
words.zh: 说实话，到…之前不太现实
words.definition: A direct but honest way to say a deadline can't be met.

examples.en: Honestly, the full system isn't realistic by Christmas.
examples.zh: 说实话，圣诞节前完成整个系统不太现实。

words.note: honestly 表示真诚。说完马上给替代方案，例如先上核心功能。

words.term: Fair enough.
words.definition: Accepts someone's point, often a criticism, calmly and without arguing.

examples.en: Fair enough, it is quite busy. I'm happy to simplify it.
examples.zh: 说得也是，确实有点乱。我可以把它简化一下。

words.note: 非常新西兰/英式的回应，表示接受但不卑不亢。

words.term: The catch is …
words.zh: 问题在于… / 麻烦的是…
words.definition: Points out the hidden downside of an idea that sounds good.

examples.en: We'd save money. The catch is we'd have nowhere to test patches.
examples.zh: 能省钱，但问题在于我们就没地方测补丁了。

words.term: If we add that, what should we take out?
words.zh: 加这个的话，要拿掉哪个？
words.definition: Pushes back on extra work by making the other person choose.

examples.en: The sprint's full. If we add that, what should we take out?
examples.zh: 迭代已经排满了。加这个的话，要拿掉哪个？

words.note: 不说“不”，而是让对方做取舍，非常有效。

words.term: I have some concerns about …
words.definition: A formal way to raise a worry, good for steering meetings and clients.

examples.en: I have some concerns about cutting over all three sites on one day.
examples.zh: 我对三个站点同一天切换有些顾虑。

words.term: Totally agree.
words.definition: A quick, strong way to show full agreement.

examples.en: Totally agree. We should add it to the change template.
examples.zh: 完全同意，应该把它加进变更模板。

words.note: 比 'I agree with you' 更口语。也可以说 'Absolutely' 或 'Spot on'。

words.term: I hear you, but …
words.definition: Shows you understand someone's feelings or pressure before you disagree.

examples.en: I hear you, but four terabytes won't copy over in one weekend.
examples.zh: 我理解，但四 TB 数据一个周末是拷不完的。

words.note: 对方情绪激动或施压时特别好用。

words.term: I see it a bit differently.
words.definition: A calm way to say you disagree, without saying the other person is wrong.

examples.en: To be honest, I see it a bit differently. The risk is the data, not the app.
examples.zh: 说实话，我的看法有点不一样。风险在数据，不在应用。

words.note: 比 'You're wrong' 柔和得多，适合对领导和客户。

words.term: That makes sense.
words.definition: Shows you understand and accept someone's reasoning.

examples.en: That makes sense. Let's go with Saturday, then.
examples.zh: 有道理，那就定周六吧。

words.term: I'm happy to …, but something else will have to give.
words.zh: 我可以做…，但别的事就得往后放
words.definition: Accepts extra work while making it clear it will affect other work.

examples.en: I'm happy to take it on, but something else will have to give.
examples.zh: 我可以接，但别的事就得往后放。

words.note: give 在这里是“让步、被牺牲”的意思。比直接拒绝更容易被接受。

words.term: I don't have that to hand, but I'll get back to you by …
words.zh: 我手头没有这个数据，…之前回复你
words.definition: Use this when someone asks for a number or detail you don't have with you.

examples.en: I don't have that number to hand, but I'll get back to you by Friday.
examples.zh: 我手头没有那个数字，周五之前回复你。

words.note: to hand = 在手边。一定要给出具体时间，不要只说 'later'。

words.term: Let me check and get back to you.
words.definition: The standard, professional answer when you don't know something yet.

examples.en: Good question. Let me check and get back to you this afternoon.
examples.zh: 好问题，我查一下，今天下午回复你。

words.note: 答不上来很正常，关键是说完一定要跟进。不要硬猜。

words.term: I'm not sure off the top of my head.
words.definition: Says you can't remember or answer right now, without sounding unprepared.

examples.en: I'm not sure off the top of my head. I'll look it up after the call.
examples.zh: 我一下子想不起来，会后我查一下。

words.note: off the top of my head = 不查资料、凭记忆。

words.term: That's not really my area, but … would know.
words.zh: 这不太是我负责的，但…应该知道
words.definition: Redirects a question to the right person without just saying 'I don't know'.

examples.en: That's not really my area, but Aroha would know.
examples.zh: 这不太是我负责的，但 Aroha 应该知道。

words.note: 说出该找谁，比单说 'I don't know' 专业得多。

words.term: Let me think about that for a sec.
words.definition: Buys you a few seconds to think before you answer.

examples.en: Hmm, let me think about that for a sec.
examples.zh: 嗯，让我想一下。

words.note: 沉默几秒是可以的，说这句就不会冷场。不要因为紧张就随便回答。

words.term: I'd rather not guess.
words.zh: 我不想随便猜（以免说错）
words.definition: Shows you care about accuracy when you don't know an answer.

examples.en: I'd rather not guess and give you the wrong number.
examples.zh: 我不想随便猜，给你一个错误的数字。

words.note: 对客户说这句显得专业可靠，而不是能力不足。

words.term: I'll find out and let you know.
words.definition: A simple promise to get the answer for someone.

examples.en: I'm not sure who owns that server. I'll find out and let you know.
examples.zh: 我不确定那台服务器归谁管，我去问一下再告诉你。

words.term: From what I know, …, but I'll double-check.
words.zh: 据我所知…，但我再核实一下
words.definition: Gives the answer you think is right while saying you'll confirm it.

examples.en: From what I know, it won't affect mobile users, but I'll double-check.
examples.zh: 据我所知不会影响手机用户，但我再核实一下。

words.note: 只知道一部分时用这个结构：说已知的，标明不确定的。

words.term: I'm not a hundred percent sure, but …
words.zh: 我不是百分之百确定，但…
words.definition: Gives your best answer while warning it might not be fully right.

examples.en: I'm not a hundred percent sure, but I think most servers are patched.
examples.zh: 我不是百分之百确定，但我觉得大部分服务器都打好补丁了。

words.term: That's my mistake.
words.definition: Admits an error simply and directly, which people respect.

examples.en: You're right, that's my mistake. I'll fix it and resend it today.
examples.zh: 你说得对，是我的错。今天改好再发一次。

words.note: 新西兰职场很欣赏直接认错。不需要长篇解释，说完马上讲怎么补救。

words.term: Actually, I need to correct what I said earlier.
words.zh: 其实我要更正一下刚才说的
words.definition: Fixes something you said wrong earlier in the same meeting.

examples.en: Actually, I need to correct what I said earlier. The cutover is the 19th.
examples.zh: 其实我要更正一下刚才说的，切换是 19 号。

words.note: 发现说错要马上更正，越晚越麻烦。

words.term: Can I come back to you on that?
words.zh: 这个我晚点回复你可以吗？
words.definition: Asks for time to answer properly instead of answering on the spot.

examples.en: Can I come back to you on that with a recommendation on Monday?
examples.zh: 这个我周一给你一个建议可以吗？

words.note: 和 'get back to you' 意思一样，都很常用。

words.term: I'll confirm that in writing.
words.definition: Promises to send the answer by email, which is useful for important details.

examples.en: I believe it's thirty days, but I'll confirm that in writing.
examples.zh: 我认为是三十天，但我会书面确认。

words.term: That was before my time.
words.definition: Explains you don't know something because it happened before you joined.

examples.en: That was before my time, but I'll check the old design docs.
examples.zh: 那是我来之前的事，但我会查一下以前的设计文档。

words.term: I'm not across …
words.zh: 我不太了解…（新西兰/澳洲口语）
words.definition: A common NZ and Australian way to say you don't know the details of something.

examples.en: I'm not across the contract side, but I'll ask our account manager.
examples.zh: 合同方面我不太了解，但我会问一下客户经理。

words.note: be across sth = 了解、掌握情况，新西兰职场非常常见。

words.term: Very roughly, …, but don't hold me to that.
words.definition: Gives a rough estimate while making clear it's not a promise.

examples.en: Very roughly, six to eight weeks, but don't hold me to that.
examples.zh: 大概六到八周，但别当成定论。

words.note: 被逼着当场估算时用，避免对方把粗估当承诺。

words.term: It's not my call, but I'll raise it with …
words.zh: 这不是我能决定的，但我会向…提出来
words.definition: Use this when someone asks for a decision you don't have the power to make.

examples.en: It's not my call, but I'll raise it with our account manager.
examples.zh: 这不是我能决定的，但我会向我们的客户经理提出来。

words.note: my call = 我的决定权。价格、折扣、合同的问题都适合这样回答。

words.term: Sorry for the delay on that.
words.definition: A short apology when you're late with something you promised.

examples.en: Sorry for the delay on that. I'm still waiting on the vendor.
examples.zh: 那件事拖了，抱歉。我还在等供应商回复。

words.term: I'll chase it up.
words.definition: Promises to follow up with someone who hasn't replied or delivered yet.

examples.en: The vendor still hasn't replied. I'll chase it up today.
examples.zh: 供应商还没回复，我今天去催一下。

words.note: chase up 是英式/新西兰常用说法，美式更常说 follow up。

words.term: It slipped through the cracks.
words.definition: An honest, light way to admit you forgot to do something.

examples.en: Sorry, it slipped through the cracks this week. I'll do it tomorrow.
examples.zh: 抱歉，这周这件事被我漏掉了，明天做。

words.term: What I can tell you is …
words.definition: Moves from what you don't know to what you do know.

examples.en: We don't know the root cause yet. What I can tell you is it started after the update.
examples.zh: 根本原因还不清楚，我能告诉你的是它是在更新之后开始的。

words.note: 故障处理时非常有用：不知道全部，也要说出已知部分。

words.term: Leave it with me.
words.definition: Tells someone you'll take care of a question or problem.

examples.en: Leave it with me. I'll have an answer for you by tomorrow.
examples.zh: 交给我吧，明天给你答复。

words.note: 很自信、很口语的说法，新西兰同事经常用。

words.term: Let me take that away.
words.definition: Says you'll look into something after the meeting instead of discussing it now.

examples.en: Good question. Let me take that away and come back to you.
examples.zh: 好问题，这个我会后研究一下再回复你。

words.note: take sth away = 带回去处理，会议上很常见。

words.term: I'll loop in …
words.zh: 我把…拉进来（邮件或讨论）
words.definition: Means you'll add someone to the email or conversation who can help.

examples.en: I'll loop in Raj from procurement. He'll know about the licences.
examples.zh: 我把采购部的 Raj 拉进来，他了解许可证的情况。

words.term: Sorry, I haven't had a chance to look at it yet.
words.definition: An honest answer when someone asks about a task you haven't started.

examples.en: Sorry, I haven't had a chance to look at it yet. I'll do it today.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我还没来得及看，今天会看。

words.note: 说完一定要给新时间。不要找很多借口。

words.term: I'll update you either way.
words.zh: 不管结果如何我都会告诉你
words.definition: Promises an update by a set time even if you don't have a final answer yet.

examples.en: I'll update you by Wednesday either way.
examples.zh: 周三之前不管结果如何我都会告诉你。

words.note: 客户最怕没消息。即使没进展也按时更新，能建立信任。

words.term: So, just to sum up, …
words.definition: Starts a short summary of the decisions at the end of a meeting.

examples.en: So, just to sum up, we're going with option B and go-live is the 15th.
examples.zh: 那我总结一下，我们选方案 B，15 号上线。

words.note: 总结时按“决定、负责人、日期”的顺序说最清楚。

words.term: I can take that.
words.definition: A quick way to volunteer for an action.

examples.en: I can take that. I'll have it done by Friday.
examples.zh: 这个我来，周五前做完。

words.note: 主动认领任务会让你在会上更有存在感。说完加上完成时间。

words.term: Who's going to own this?
words.definition: Asks who is responsible for an action, so it doesn't get forgotten.

examples.en: Great idea. Who's going to own this?
examples.zh: 好主意，这件事谁来负责？

words.note: own = 负责到底。比 'Who will do it?' 更职场化。

words.term: Can we put a name and a date against that?
words.zh: 这件事能定个负责人和日期吗？
words.definition: Pushes the group to give an action an owner and a deadline.

examples.en: Before we go, can we put a name and a date against that?
examples.zh: 散会前，这件事能定个负责人和日期吗？

words.term: Shall we park that for now?
words.definition: Suggests stopping a side discussion and coming back to it later.

examples.en: Good point, but shall we park that for now and come back to it next week?
examples.zh: 说得好，但这个先放一放，下周再讨论？

words.note: park = 暂时搁置。会议跑题时非常常用、不得罪人。

words.term: Let's take that offline.
words.definition: Moves a detailed or difficult discussion out of the meeting to a smaller group.

examples.en: Let's take that offline. I'll set up a call with both teams.
examples.zh: 这个会后单独讨论吧，我约两个团队开个会。

words.note: offline 这里不是“断网”，是“会后私下”。

words.term: I'll send round the notes.
words.zh: 我会把会议纪要发给大家
words.definition: Promises to share the meeting notes or actions with everyone.

examples.en: Thanks, everyone. I'll send round the notes this afternoon.
examples.zh: 谢谢大家，我今天下午把纪要发给大家。

words.note: send round / send out 都可以。也可说 circulate the minutes（更正式）。

words.term: I'll follow up with an email.
words.definition: Promises written details after the meeting.

examples.en: I'll follow up with an email listing the decisions and owners.
examples.zh: 我会后发邮件，列出决定事项和负责人。

words.term: What are the next steps?
words.definition: Asks what will happen after the meeting and who will do it.

examples.en: Okay, so what are the next steps from here?
examples.zh: 好，那接下来怎么做？

words.note: 会议结束前如果没人说下一步，就主动问这句。

words.term: So the action is on …
words.definition: Confirms out loud who owns an action.

examples.en: So the action is on Tom to check the network by Thursday.
examples.zh: 那这项任务由 Tom 负责，周四前查网络。

words.term: We're nearly out of time.
words.definition: Warns the group that the meeting is about to end.

examples.en: We're nearly out of time, so let's agree the actions.
examples.zh: 我们时间快到了，先把任务定下来吧。

words.term: Let's pick this up next week.
words.definition: Moves an unfinished topic to a future meeting.

examples.en: We won't solve it today. Let's pick this up next week.
examples.zh: 今天解决不了，下周再接着讨论。

words.note: pick up = 接着继续。

words.term: Does that work for everyone?
words.definition: Checks that a time, plan or decision is okay with the whole group.

examples.en: Same time next Tuesday. Does that work for everyone?
examples.zh: 下周二同一时间，大家都可以吗？

words.term: I think that's everything.
words.definition: Signals that the meeting has covered all its topics.

examples.en: I think that's everything. Thanks for your time, everyone.
examples.zh: 我想就这些了，谢谢大家抽时间。

words.term: Anything else before we wrap up?
words.definition: Gives people a last chance to raise something before the meeting ends.

examples.en: Anything else before we wrap up?
examples.zh: 结束前还有别的吗？

words.note: wrap up = 收尾、结束。主持会议时必备。

words.term: Thanks, everyone. That was really useful.
words.definition: A warm, simple way to close a meeting.

examples.en: Thanks, everyone. That was really useful. Have a good afternoon.
examples.zh: 谢谢大家，很有收获。下午愉快。

words.term: Just so nothing gets missed, …
words.definition: A friendly reason to confirm owners and dates for actions.

examples.en: Just so nothing gets missed, who's taking the backup alerts?
examples.zh: 为了不遗漏，备份告警谁来跟？

words.term: Where did we land on …?
words.definition: Asks what was finally decided about a topic.

examples.en: Where did we land on the database question?
examples.zh: 数据库那个问题最后是怎么定的？

words.note: land 在这里是“得出结论”，很地道的口语。

words.term: Let's make a call on … by …
words.zh: 我们在…之前把…定下来吧
words.definition: Sets a deadline for a decision so work isn't blocked.

examples.en: Let's make a call on the storage option by next Friday.
examples.zh: 我们下周五之前把存储方案定下来吧。

words.note: make a call = 做决定。

words.term: I can help with that, but I can't own it.
words.zh: 我可以帮忙，但不能负责到底
words.definition: Offers support without becoming the person responsible.

examples.en: I can help with that, but I can't own it this month.
examples.zh: 我可以帮忙，但这个月没法负责到底。

words.note: 避免任务全落到你身上的好办法。

words.term: Let's agree on the actions before we go.
words.zh: 散会前把任务定下来吧
words.definition: Makes sure the meeting ends with clear actions, not just discussion.

examples.en: We've got five minutes. Let's agree on the actions before we go.
examples.zh: 还有五分钟，散会前把任务定下来吧。

words.term: I'll set up a follow-up meeting.
words.zh: 我来安排一次后续会议
words.definition: Offers to book another meeting to continue the discussion.

examples.en: I'll set up a follow-up meeting with the security team.
examples.zh: 我来和安全团队安排一次后续会议。

words.note: set up a meeting = 约会议。不要说 'make a meeting'。

words.term: Can we add that to next week's agenda?
words.zh: 能把这个放进下周的议程吗？
words.definition: Moves a new topic to a later meeting instead of discussing it now.

examples.en: That's a good one. Can we add that to next week's agenda?
examples.zh: 这个问题很好，能放进下周的议程吗？

words.term: Let's give everyone a few minutes back.
words.definition: A friendly way to end a meeting early.

examples.en: We're done early, so let's give everyone a few minutes back.
examples.zh: 我们提前讲完了，那就提早几分钟结束吧。

words.note: 很受欢迎的一句话，大家都喜欢会议提前结束。

words.term: We'll leave it there.
words.definition: A clear, polite way to finish a meeting.

examples.en: Okay, we'll leave it there. Thanks, everyone.
examples.zh: 好，今天就到这里，谢谢大家。

words.term: When can we expect an update?
words.zh: 什么时候能有进展更新？
words.definition: Asks the owner of an action when they'll report back.

examples.en: Thanks, Tom. When can we expect an update?
examples.zh: 谢谢 Tom，什么时候能有进展更新？

words.note: 你的工作依赖别人时一定要问，不然只能干等。

words.term: Sorry, I was on mute.
words.definition: The most common thing said on video calls, after people talk without unmuting.

examples.en: Sorry, I was on mute. Can you hear me now?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我刚才静音了。现在能听到吗？

words.note: on mute 用介词 on。不要说 'I was muted myself'。

words.term: You're on mute.
words.definition: Tells someone their microphone is off while they're talking.

examples.en: Raj, I think you're on mute.
examples.zh: Raj，你好像静音了。

words.note: 加 I think 更客气。

words.term: Can you see my screen?
words.definition: Checks that your screen share is working.

examples.en: Okay, can you see my screen?
examples.zh: 好，能看到我的屏幕吗？

words.term: We can't see your screen yet.
words.zh: 我们还看不到你的屏幕
words.definition: Tells the presenter their screen share isn't showing.

examples.en: Sorry, we can't see your screen yet. It's still loading.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我们还看不到你的屏幕，还在加载。

words.term: Is it coming through okay?
words.zh: 显示正常吗？/ 能看到吗？
words.definition: Checks that your screen, audio or video is reaching the others.

examples.en: Let me try sharing again. Is it coming through okay?
examples.zh: 我再共享一次。显示正常吗？

words.note: come through = 传过去。屏幕、声音都可以用。

words.term: You're breaking up a bit.
words.zh: 你的声音有点断断续续
words.definition: Tells someone their audio is unclear because of a bad connection.

examples.en: Sorry, Aroha, you're breaking up a bit.
examples.zh: 抱歉，Aroha，你的声音有点断断续续。

words.note: break up = 信号断续，不是“分手”。

words.term: Sorry, I dropped out. What did I miss?
words.zh: 抱歉我掉线了，刚才错过了什么？
words.definition: Use this when you rejoin a call after losing your connection.

examples.en: Sorry, I dropped out for a minute. What did I miss?
examples.zh: 抱歉我掉线了一分钟，刚才错过了什么？

words.note: drop out / drop off 都表示掉线。

words.term: My internet's playing up.
words.definition: A casual NZ and British way to say your connection isn't working well.

examples.en: Sorry, my internet's playing up today. I'll turn my camera off.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我今天网络有点问题，我把摄像头关了。

words.note: play up = （机器）出毛病，新西兰非常常用。

words.term: I'll keep my camera off, if that's okay.
words.zh: 我先不开摄像头，可以吗？
words.definition: Politely explains you won't use video, usually because of bandwidth.

examples.en: My connection's slow, so I'll keep my camera off, if that's okay.
examples.zh: 我网速慢，先不开摄像头，可以吗？

words.note: 跟客户开会最好开摄像头；实在不行就先说明原因。

words.term: Sorry I'm late. My last meeting ran over.
words.zh: 抱歉迟到了，上一个会拖堂了
words.definition: The most common, accepted reason for joining a call late.

examples.en: Hi, sorry I'm late. My last meeting ran over. Please carry on.
examples.zh: 嗨，抱歉迟到了，上一个会拖堂了。大家继续。

words.note: run over = 超时。道歉一句就够了，不要打断会议解释太多。

words.term: No, you go.
words.definition: Use this when you and someone else start talking at the same moment on a call.

examples.en: Oh, no, you go. I'll jump in after.
examples.zh: 哦，不不，你先说，我等下再说。

words.note: 网络延迟时经常发生，笑一下很自然。

words.term: Can everyone hear me okay?
words.zh: 大家都能听清我说话吗？
words.definition: Checks your audio at the start of a call or after changing devices.

examples.en: Hi all, can everyone hear me okay?
examples.zh: 大家好，都能听清我说话吗？

words.term: Let me share my screen.
words.definition: Tells everyone you're about to show something on your screen.

examples.en: It's easier to show you. Let me share my screen.
examples.zh: 直接给你们看更清楚，我来共享一下屏幕。

words.term: You should see … now.
words.zh: 你们现在应该能看到…了
words.definition: Tells people what's on your shared screen before you explain it.

examples.en: Okay, you should see the dashboard now.
examples.zh: 好，你们现在应该能看到仪表板了。

words.term: I'll walk you through it.
words.definition: Says you'll explain something step by step, often while sharing your screen.

examples.en: This is the new design. I'll walk you through it from left to right.
examples.zh: 这是新设计，我从左到右带大家过一遍。

words.note: 讲解时说清你在看哪里：'at the top', 'on the left', 'the red bar'。

words.term: I'll pop it in the chat.
words.definition: Says you'll type a link, name or question in the meeting chat.

examples.en: I'll pop the link in the chat now.
examples.zh: 我现在把链接发到聊天框里。

words.note: pop = 随手放，新西兰口语很常用。

words.term: Could you zoom in a bit?
words.definition: Asks the presenter to make their screen easier to read.

examples.en: Could you zoom in a bit? The text's quite small.
examples.zh: 能放大一点吗？字有点小。

words.term: I'll have to drop off at …
words.definition: Tells the group early that you need to leave before the end.

examples.en: Just a heads-up, I'll have to drop off at ten past.
examples.zh: 先说一下，我十分的时候得先退出会议。

words.note: 最好在会议开始时就说，并请大家先讨论你负责的部分。

words.term: Sorry, wrong screen.
words.definition: A quick apology when you share the wrong window.

examples.en: Oops, sorry, wrong screen. Let me switch to the slides.
examples.zh: 哎呀，抱歉，共享错屏幕了，我切到幻灯片。

words.note: 共享前关掉不相关的窗口和通知，避免尴尬。

words.term: Could everyone mute if they're not talking?
words.zh: 不发言的时候大家能静音吗？
words.definition: A polite request to reduce background noise, without blaming one person.

examples.en: There's a bit of noise. Could everyone mute if they're not talking?
examples.zh: 有点杂音，不发言的时候大家能静音吗？

words.note: 对所有人说，不点名，就不会让人尴尬。

words.term: I've just put my hand up.
words.definition: Tells the host you've used the raise-hand button and want to speak.

examples.en: Sarah, I've just put my hand up, if there's time.
examples.zh: Sarah，我刚举手了，如果还有时间的话。

words.note: 人多的线上会议里，举手功能是插话的好办法。

words.term: There's a bit of a lag.
words.definition: Explains a delay in the audio or video that makes conversation awkward.

examples.en: Sorry, there's a bit of a lag on my end.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我这边有点延迟。

words.note: on my end / on your end = 我这边/你那边。

words.term: It's quite hard to hear the room from here.
words.zh: 在线上听不太清会议室里的声音
words.definition: Use this in hybrid meetings when you're online and the people in the room are hard to hear.

examples.en: Sorry, it's quite hard to hear the room from here. Could you move closer to the mic?
examples.zh: 抱歉，线上听不太清会议室的声音，能靠近麦克风一点吗？

words.note: 混合会议中线上的人很容易被忽视，要主动说出来。

words.term: Could you go back a slide?
words.definition: Asks the presenter to show the previous slide again.

examples.en: Sorry, could you go back a slide? I wanted to ask about the costs.
examples.zh: 抱歉，能回到上一页吗？我想问一下费用。

words.term: Bear with me a sec.
words.definition: Asks people to wait while you fix something, like a slow screen share.

examples.en: Bear with me a sec, Teams is being a bit slow.
examples.zh: 稍等一下，Teams 有点卡。

words.note: bear with me = 请耐心等我一下，非常常用。不要写成 bare。

words.term: Your video's frozen.
words.definition: Tells someone their camera picture has stopped moving.

examples.en: Raj, your video's frozen, but we can still hear you.
examples.zh: Raj，你的画面卡住了，不过还能听到你声音。

words.term: We lost you for a minute there.
words.zh: 刚才有一会儿没你的声音了
words.definition: Tells someone their connection dropped for a short time.

examples.en: We lost you for a minute there. Could you go back to the backup part?
examples.zh: 刚才有一会儿没你的声音了，能从备份那部分再讲一下吗？

words.term: Where did I cut out?
words.definition: Asks what the others last heard, so you can continue from the right place.

examples.en: Sorry, my connection dropped. Where did I cut out?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我掉线了。我是从哪里断掉的？
